items.title: Barney Bigard Interview, Early 1970s
items.q: The interviewer addresses the interviewee as 'Marnie Begard', but the interviewee (Barney Bigard) never confirms this name nor discusses any relationship with a person named Marnie Begard.

ctx.x: It was made with, uh, made in Chicago, with a guy named, uh, My Knee Jones, he was a peg-legged pianist. Mm-hm. And, uh, well, in fact, when I went to Chicago, and I was supposed to go to work with King Alva, it was near the end, and the place where we were going to work, we were supposed to start on the Christmas Eve, and it burned down. Mm-hm. So we were sort of stranded. And this, uh, fellow, My Knee Jones, he was from New Orleans, and he was a writer, composer. And he had little gigs, and he found out that we…
What was it that inspired you to go into music, Marnie Begard?

Me? Well, I wanted to, truthfully, I wanted to be a trumpet player. Really? And, uh, because, and then I could whistle good. So the, the, the old folks, you know, they said, well, the sun is too much wind. You can't blow that kind of horses. I want to try the clarinet. So, uh, I said, okay. So, uh, I said, okay. So, my uncle was a fiddle player, Emil Begard. A fiddle player? Yeah. He used to lead a band. He used to lead Kid Overs band into that. Uh-huh. And, uh, Baby Daz was the clarinetist. And in those, those…
